representation_notes: Use one Fourier coefficient representation Coeff = ℤ → ℂ, with MemH s the summability of (1+k²)^s |f_k|², and hn its square-root sum. It is the specified completion of Fourier polynomials, not a strengthened solution space. HB includes MemH, so totalized real tsums never certify regularity by themselves. Source homogeneous norms delete frequency zero. RealField is f(-k)=conj(f(k)); ZeroMean is f(0)=0. Product is coefficient convolution. S has multiplier exp(i t k³); inverse derivatives kill zero. The four terms of Htau, including its finite 1/τ coefficient, are copied exactly; numerical uses ordinary finite function iteration without cutoff. Time integrals are coefficientwise complex Bochner interval integrals. ContH explicitly gives norm continuity on the closed interval. Weak is the coefficientwise distributional time derivative, tested against compactly supported smooth real scalar functions; EssBound includes measurability, Sobolev membership almost everywhere and finite essential supremum. XPath uses weak derivatives; Xnorm uses essential suprema, while UB and SupH use continuous representatives. Piecewise records a finite set of breakpoints with smooth pieces and globally continuous spatial Sobolev paths; derivatives at finitely many joins have no effect on Weak or Xnorm. KSol is the integrated twisted Fourier equation, equivalent for continuous L² paths to the distributional physical equation by Fourier testing; no second physical Lean representation is introduced. Exact adds uniqueness and uniform H^s approximation by solutions with Fourier-truncated data. T013 supplies a checked weighted lp₂ realization only as reusable Hilbert-space infrastructure for truncation, inclusions and completion; FromLP is an explicit invertible positive Fourier weight, not an assumed capability. The pinned lp parameter 2 is the ℝ≥0∞ summability exponent (not a regularity index); real Sobolev order s stays in the weight. iteratedDerivWithin uses a natural derivative order and the actual closed interval. n2 is the maximum of pairwise minima (second largest magnitude), n3 the minimum of pairwise maxima (third largest), including ties. N in cutoff/high is a real frequency threshold, not an integer index. Nat L,n are step counts/indices and their real casts are explicit. E003-E005 keep the factor sqrt(2π) in source norms; E004/E005 quantify an admissibility threshold for positive epsilon, with constants chosen after epsilon and before time/input data. Each constant existential is outside the data, time-grid and Fourier-support quantifiers it must be uniform over. Original T,gamma,R and H001-H003 are unchanged and universally closed by the interface parameters; all E ports retain their full source signatures. Background notes remain optional references, never premise ports. Estimates, completion, reflection, endpoint matching and all operator-extension properties remain proof obligations; the header proves none. The plan has twelve distinct source-output steps, one shared Sobolev implementation bridge, and four independently usable subarguments; source paragraph coverage is explicit in each step. BilinearExtensions, TriExtensions and StageExtensions state convergence of the actual polynomial/path approximations to the defined output, rather than presupposing a bounded extension. XConvergence requires genuine XPath membership of every difference and convergence in its finite controlling norm; the path extension is only for approximable paths. AccResidual explicitly retains the interpolant's continuous piecewise smooth, real mean-zero status for downstream normal forms. LinftyBound asserts boundedness of the Fourier representative's range as well as the supremum estimate. The repaired time regularity order is explicitly ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) in both Weak and SmoothOn: the inner top denotes unbounded finite differentiability order, then is coerced into ContDiff's WithTop ℕ∞ order type. The outer top of that type denotes analyticity and is not used for either predicate. Inspected pinned FTaylorSeries.lean:112-120 and Defs.lean:549-550,1115-1116 identify this smooth order with every finite natural derivative order. Thus Weak tests against all compactly supported C∞ real scalar functions, including nonzero bumps in the open interval; its derivative argument is constrained by genuine distributional integration by parts. SmoothOn and Piecewise allow arbitrary C∞ time coefficients with the stated Sobolev derivative continuity, including smooth nonanalytic paths. EFlow/SourceApprox and Exact/SmoothApprox consequently require only the source smooth approximation. This is a repair of the time-order encoding after located semantic feedback, with no new root assumption, analytic premise or changed NL0 route.

steps.explanation: Shared implementation of the existing weighted Fourier completion arguments: realize H^s by the explicit weight in lp₂, identify its norm, prove convergence of Fourier truncations, monotone Sobolev inclusions and completeness. Inspected pinned lp.norm_eq_tsum_rpow has premise 0 < p.toReal and exponent p : ℝ≥0∞; here p=2. This is a derived bridge using definitions and Mathlib, with no new H or background premise.

Apply the source flows to U₀(k)=-f(-k), reflect back, and prove the equation, reality and norm identities coefficientwise. Keep the constants uniform on the ball. Use source uniqueness across regularities for smooth data, and theta=0 in E002 for all L² pairs with norm sum ≤2R. The reflected integrated Fourier equation is the physical KdV distributional equation on continuous L² paths; smooth approximation is in uniform H^gamma norm. Twisting is an isometry. No source proof body is an input. In SmoothOn the order is explicitly the coerced top of ℕ∞, so the higher-Sobolev equation argument must establish each finite time derivative and its Sobolev continuity. It need not establish time analyticity; this also gives precisely the SmoothApprox/SourceApprox regularity.

Prove the covariance zero case, elementary small-phase estimate and integration by parts ratio estimate; interchange alpha,beta and retain both minima. This step is independent of the PDE and E roots.

Use zero-sum frequency orderings for the two pointwise majorants. Follow the existing dyadic proof: comparable top shells, Cauchy-Schwarz on the two large inputs, counting on smaller shells, then sum the geometric offset. Extend nonnegative finite restrictions by their supremum, proving summability. Encoding d=-a-b-c is a bijective indexing of the zero-sum hyperplane; A is an arbitrary interaction subset.

Apply the covariance bounds and the two four-frequency majorants to alpha=3ab(a+b), beta=3kc(a+b), d=-k. Geometrically interpolate the two existing endpoints, treating sigma=0,1 explicitly; keep all nonzero-frequency and a+b guards.

Dualize on finite Fourier supports and apply the positive four-linear bound, including every extra multiplier of modulus ≤1. Prove absolute coefficient convergence, bounded trilinearity, unique dense-core extension and the uniform bound. For the mixed endpoint, expand the difference at (f,f,f) and (w,w,w) into the three existing telescoping terms and use sigma=0 on them. No H^sigma hypothesis is placed on f.

Prove the supplied inverse-derivative, H¹ algebra, B, J and asymmetric J estimates from Fourier Cauchy-Schwarz and products. pstar=23/14 is strictly greater than 3/2. linfty is the supremum of the continuous Fourier representative, whose absolute/uniform convergence follows from the inverse-derivative bound. Establish density compatibility of these bounded products.

Retain the previously proved bounds and prove the normal-form identities by differentiating the explicit oscillatory J coefficient on smooth inputs. Justify termwise differentiation by rapid Fourier decay. Integrate with both endpoints; continuous finite pieces telescope. Derive the J(B,h)=Ctri identity and the constant-input first-stage identity, extending the latter by Fourier truncation. SmoothOn and Piecewise now use C∞ order ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞); all source smooth time paths, including nonanalytic ones, remain in the domain of the normal form. Termwise differentiation uses the existing smooth Sobolev/Fourier bounds.

Show that continuous piecewise smooth paths have the specified weak derivatives, with cancellation at all joins. Apply E003 for every negative-norm slot at alpha=0, and to constant H^sigma inputs at alpha=sigma. Divide the source norms by sqrt(2π), changing only constants. Prove the stated density extensions in controlling norms; path density is only in the closure of the initial smooth domain, not the whole X space. Weak now tests against arbitrary compactly supported C∞ scalar functions using order ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞). Prove the actual integration-by-parts identity on each smooth piece and cancel matching endpoint terms; this supplies the genuine weak derivative required by E003. The pinned contDiff_infty/contDiffOn_infty equivalences and C∞ bump APIs were inspected, with explicit order/field/function/set arguments checked. No analytic path hypothesis is needed.

For gamma away from 1/2 use E005 with its exact source exponent. At gamma=1/2 choose a permitted positive epsilon ≤1/8 from the existential threshold, then use H^(1/8)→H^epsilon. Normalize the bilinear norms. Prove ag(gamma)∈[0,1) with exactly the three specified cases; no gamma=0 product clause is introduced.

Retain normalized trilinear and product estimates. Choose the permitted E004 epsilon independently of stage data. Derive the time-shift covariance from the explicit S multipliers and apply E004 at n=0 to S_a w. Check all beta interval conditions and positive denominators. The three source powers at beta=ag are ≥gamma, while beta=1+gamma gives power zero. Extend both target Sobolev estimates by the same polynomial sequence, so their distributional values agree. Constants precede a,t,tau,w.

Use the H¹ algebra and inverse derivatives to prove continuity of every update term at a fixed positive timestep, reality/mean preservation, smoothness and finite-iterate continuity. Apply E006 with exactly the unfiltered psi. Calculate Vst at both endpoints and prove they match adjacent twisted states; consequently the explicit floor-index interpolation is continuous and piecewise smooth, including its final endpoint. No timestep-uniform Lipschitz property of psi is asserted.

Under StepData follow the seven existing Interp formulas. Compare F(f) with F(w) by bilinearity of J; use the two distinct stage Sobolev bounds for B(F,F). Bound W by the mixed remainder endpoint. For Dinv B(f,F), split f=w+(f-w). Use the normal form for Cst, then the three-term trilinear difference at w. Derive Y', inverse-derivative and X estimates. All constants are uniform in higher norms of f and Fourier support.

Differentiate the actual stage interpolation, obtain rho' and apply the two-endpoint normal form to B(Y,z) and B(Y,Y). Assign the negative Sobolev slot to Y in the remaining cubic term. Concatenate the explicit residual increments; weak derivatives ignore only finitely many grid joins. On any grid-started interval, including a partial last step, at most h/tau+1 increments occur and delta_n≤E_I. Prove accumulated residual and error X bounds with these exact constants. The AccResidual Weak field now quantifies all compactly supported C∞ scalar tests, so prove the concatenated weak equation by integration by parts with cancellation of the continuous interpolation's endpoint contributions. Values of the ordinary derivative at the finite grid join set do not affect the integrals or essential norms; a jump in the path itself cannot be discarded.

Follow the accepted low/high proof. Use the exact error identity and inverse-product low-frequency estimate. Keep both endpoints of the normal form. In cubic terms telescope three projections to put a high input in one slot and apply the negative-norm estimate there. For the forcing integral substitute the actual stepwise rho', rather than estimating an arbitrary forcing. Sum partial-step bounds. Choose a common N0,delta,K only after the uniform constants and absorb the E_I coefficient. Export every displayed pre-absorption estimate as well as the short-interval inequality.

Choose the exact-flow ball bound and M0 before the initial datum, then choose the common stability constants. Divide the grid into blocks of m=floor(delta/tau) steps; include a possibly shorter final block. Iterate the restarted bound and close the first-exit bootstrap using continuity. Retain both the full interpolated-time bound and the grid error by unitarity, uniformly in the entire smooth-data ball.

Choose the smooth-data constants first. Approximate arbitrary data by real mean-zero Fourier projections staying in the same H^gamma ball. The exact solutions converge uniformly in L² by T001, and numerical iterates converge at every grid point by fixed-timestep finite-iterate continuity in T007. Pass the inequality to the limit over the finite grid, preserving exactly C,tau0 and the full original quantifier order. Exact includes the unique continuous distributional solution obtained by smooth approximation; GridError includes that every iterate is real mean-zero L².
